channel.title: Product Diary
channel.description: What changed across the projects, day by day.

item.title: Epochs of Power Research Lands as SnapDog Gets a Slide
item.description: A paperwork day: my Epochs of Power game research was saved to git, SnapDog got a one-slide story, and Lectern's ads were corrected.

item.title: Epochs of Power Records Where the Old Game Decides Ties
item.description: My strategy-game research gained a long set of written findings about Call to Power II, plus scripts that watch the original game run.

item.title: Grok Bot Notes Record a Quiet Day and a Mac Mini Back Online
item.description: The notes on my fleet of assistants recorded no changes to any bot, and noted that the Mac mini reconnected after a day offline.

item.title: Hermes Fleet Misses the Same Laptop for a Sixth Morning
item.description: My house assistant's overnight head-count again could not find one laptop, and my NAS now has less spare memory than at any earlier check.

item.title: Lectern Gets Ad Copy That Matches What the Store Sells
item.description: The Mac app itself did not change; I wrote new ad copy after finding my own notes undersold what the store version already does.

item.title: SnapDog Gets a One-Slide Story of Its Road to the Store
item.description: The app itself was unchanged, but I added a one-slide summary of how it went from idea to the Mac App Store.

item.title: Dead Signal's Book Page Gets Tracking and a New Sample Address
item.description: The Dead Signal pages on my books site now report where visitors came from, and the opening sample has moved to a new address.

item.title: Dead Signal Gets Ad Tracking as SnapDog Notes Get Fixed
item.description: Dead Signal's book pages learned to track where ad visitors come from, and my own SnapDog notes turned out to be wrong about its release.

item.title: Hermes Fleet Misses the Same Laptop for a Fifth Morning
item.description: My house assistant's overnight head-count again could not reach one laptop, and the spare memory on my NAS fell to its lowest figure so far.

item.title: Remnant Academy Gets a Tax Switch and a Payment Fix
item.description: The academy's checkout can now collect sales tax once I switch it on, and a payment-recording check that could hide failures was tightened.

item.title: SnapDog Gets New Ad Research After Its Own Notes Were Wrong
item.description: The app did not change, but I wrote new ad copy for SnapDog after finding my own notes still called the shipped app unreleased.

item.title: SnapDog Gets a First Demo Film as Hermes Fleet Fails
item.description: SnapDog, my Mac screenshot app, now has a two-minute silent demo film for its website, while my house assistant failed its morning check again.

item.title: Grok Bot Notes Record Eleven Assistants Renamed in a Day
item.description: The notes on my fleet of assistants noted that eleven bots were renamed with a new title style, and that no new bots appeared.

item.title: Hermes Fleet Fails Its Morning Check for a Fourth Day
item.description: My house assistant's morning health report failed again and its head-count still cannot reach one laptop, but the other three machines answered normally.

item.title: SnapDog Gets a First Silent Film Cut for Its Website
item.description: The first complete demo film for SnapDog's website exists as a silent two-minute story, and the notes say plainly which features it does not yet prove.

item.title: Hermes Fleet Misses a Laptop as Grok Bot Adds Two Bots
item.description: A quiet Monday: SnapDog's old proof files went into version control, Hermes Fleet lost a laptop again, and Grok Bot's notes caught up.

item.title: Grok Bot Documents Two New Assistants After a Missed Week
item.description: The house notes for my fleet of assistants caught up after five days without a refresh and added two new bots, one for election mail and one for phone calls.

item.title: Hermes Fleet Recounts the House and Still Misses a Laptop
item.description: My house assistant's overnight head-count still cannot reach one laptop, and its morning health report failed again because the model server stayed silent.

item.title: SnapDog Files Its Scrolling-Capture Proof and Two Decks
item.description: The app did not change; I filed the proof that scrolling capture works, my demo-film shoot notes and two slide decks telling its story.

item.title: Hermes WebUI Went Live and the Fleet Lost Its Voice
item.description: My house assistant put a web front-end on my private network in eight minutes, while its morning health report failed and its evening voice crashed.

item.title: Hermes Fleet Loses Its Voice and a Laptop Stays Missing
item.description: The house assistant's morning health report failed and its evening spoken summary crashed outright, while the overnight head-count still misses one laptop.

item.title: Hermes WebUI Gives My House Assistant a Screen of Its Own
item.description: The house assistant installed a browser front-end for itself tonight and had it answering on my phone within eight minutes.

item.title: Lightfence's Mac Steam Candidate Is Built and Recorded
item.description: A complete unsigned Mac build of the puzzle game now exists as a Steam candidate, and its build record landed in the repository tonight.

item.title: SnapDog Stops One Blank Frame From Killing a Recording
item.description: A Mac screen recording could be ruined by a single empty frame; SnapDog now drops those frames and the recording survives.

item.title: Epochs of Power Opponent Stops Peeking at Your Units
item.description: The computer opponent in my strategy prototype no longer sees the whole map, so it now has to scout like a player would.

item.title: A Fire TV Stick Loses Its Trackers, With an Undo Button
item.description: I started stripping tracking and advertising services off a streaming stick, with backups and a one-command way to put everything back.

item.title: My Assistant Now Picks Which Model Does Each Job
item.description: My assistant can hand a job to a different model depending on the work, from one running on my own desk to a paid cloud one, and the last route took two false starts to get working.

item.title: Hermes Fleet Notices That One Computer Has Gone Missing
item.description: My house assistant re-checked which computers it can reach overnight and found one of them no longer answers to its name.

item.title: Night Chorus TV Version Now Shares One Purchase
item.description: Night Chorus, the crystal game formerly called Prism Shift, now uses one identity across all its Apple versions, so a single purchase should cover them.

item.title: Lightfence Stops Crashing When the Sound Fails to Start
item.description: Lightfence could quit on its own if the phone's audio was busy when a sound played, and that crash is now fixed.

item.title: AdGenerator Now Feeds on LaunchDeck's Recordings
item.description: The ad pipeline can now pull its footage straight from LaunchDeck's recordings of the real apps, with no copying files by hand between the two tools.

item.title: The Build Fleet Learns Windows and Stops Losing Job Receipts
item.description: The build system that spreads my compiling work across the house added a Windows worker, kept receipts when connections dropped, and showed memory pressure.

item.title: Epochs of Power Probes Call to Power II Without a Screen
item.description: My research project toward a touch-first historical strategy game spent the day documenting the 2000 original and probing it automatically without a display.

item.title: Teaching My Assistant to Survey the House and Read Aloud
item.description: My assistant can now check which of my computers are awake, work out where each job should run, and speak a spoken summary of long answers as a playable recording.

item.title: Hermes Fleet Takes Stock of the House and Reads Answers Aloud
item.description: My house assistant can now survey which computers are awake, and read long answers aloud as recordings that refuse to say anything the written answer did not.

item.title: Hisense Podcasts Gets a Native Library and Clearer Controls
item.description: My television's podcasts app now puts private subscriptions beside regular shows, remembers older episodes, and makes its buttons easier to see.

item.title: Hisense Podcasts Gets a Native Library That Refreshes Itself
item.description: The Hisense television's podcasts app now keeps one native library of ordinary and paid private shows, reaches older episodes, and refreshes itself on launch.

item.title: LaunchDeck Learns All Thirty-Three Apps and Films Godot Too
item.description: My marketing pipeline tool now knows all thirty-three of my apps and games as build-and-film recipes, including games made in the Godot engine.

item.title: Let Me Retire Publishes One Dream, One Button and No Payments
item.description: I published a one-page joke site called Let Me Retire: one dream, one million dollars, one button, and a checkout that honestly reports it is not configured.

item.title: Meshy's 3D Pipeline Gets a Manual and a Real Audit
item.description: The toolbox that turns text into three-dimensional models got a single manual for every coding assistant, plus an audit that verified what it can really do.

item.title: Pipe Flow's Website Now Plays Three Boards in the Browser
item.description: The Pipe Flow website gained a playable three-board demo built from the game's own art and sound, and the game itself gained tests and a Linux build script.

item.title: Night Chorus Gets a Release Path, and Alerts Reach My Phone
item.description: One Friday of plumbing: failures now reach my phone, a skipped night cannot hide, and Night Chorus's first release check found four problems in seconds.

item.title: Night Chorus Builds for Steam and Fails Its Own Release Check
item.description: Night Chorus, the crystal game formerly called Prism Shift, built a Linux candidate for Steam and wrote itself a release checklist that failed its first run.

item.title: Lightfence 1.3 Repaints Its Art and Its Site Says Out Now
item.description: Lightfence's next version repaints every picture in the game at high resolution with shimmering gems, and its website now carries the store badge.

item.title: SnapDog Rewrites Its Website Films Around Remote Help
item.description: The Mac app's help menu now opens the SnapDog website, and the site's demo films were re-planned twice to tell one story about helping someone remotely.

item.title: YOLK SOULS Rewrites Its README to Match the Real Game
item.description: The hop-and-die adventure game's project card now describes the playable build that exists, not the month-old design it had outgrown.

item.title: Pipe Flow's Desktop Audit Found Leaks 34 Seconds Early
item.description: Checking Pipe Flow's desktop port against the phone game found leaks bursting early on 111 of 140 levels, while Lightfence, SnapDog and StatBar also moved.

item.title: Hisense Podcasts Gains Private Feeds and Remote Navigation
item.description: The television's podcasts app gained private show feeds, working remote navigation and a Now Playing card on the home screen.

item.title: Pipe Flow on Desktop Catches Up With the Phone Game
item.description: The desktop version of Pipe Flow was brought much closer to the phone game in feel, sound, menus and 13 languages.

item.title: Lightfence Gets a Tabletop Layout for Folding Phones
item.description: Lightfence gained a tabletop layout for a folding phone, and build 1004 went to App Store review.
